title: EMV Chip Data Example
applicability: Applies to EMV transactions where Segment 100 is accompanied by required Segment 130 EMV Request Data.

businessRequirements.title: An EMV Segment 100 transaction shall include Segment 130 EMV Request Data in Data Section 3.
EMV Chip Data shall begin with a valid three-digit length consistent with the following encoded chip data.
EMV Chip Data shall preserve valid BCD-packed/hex TLV tag, length, and value structure.
EMV chip values such as authorized amount, transaction type, currency, and terminal country shall agree with the Segment 100 transaction context.

testCases.positive: EMV tags agree with Segment 100 context

testData.reason: Segment 130 presence and Element 63 count are structural checks; synthetic placeholder chip data is sufficient.
Length-prefix validation is structural; does not require a genuine EMV card/kernel.
BCD/hex TLV tag-length-value framing is structural and synthesizable.
Amount/currency/transaction-type cross-check compares plaintext TLV values against Segment 100 fields; no cryptographic verification involved.

No current BR claims cryptographic verification of the 9F26 Application Cryptogram (ARQC/TC); genuine verification requires a certified EMV kernel or HSM and cannot be synthesized. Tracked here so this boundary is explicit if such a BR is added later.

testDataReadinessSummary.note: All defined BRs validate structural/plaintext TLV content and are synthesizable. Cryptogram authenticity is out of scope and explicitly flagged as external-fixture-required.

testDataStatus: Segment 130 presence and Element 63 compatibility are covered; complete EMV TLV and cross-field validation remains pending as synthetic data, not a cryptographic gap. Cryptogram authenticity (9F26) is explicitly out of scope pending a certified EMV kernel/HSM fixture.
